name: Jeff Merkley

issue_poll.name: OPB Fall 2026 Election Survey (DHM Research), Sept 17-27, 2026, 915 likely voters (1,000 registered)
issue_poll.note: Ranked by the open-ended 'most important problem facing Oregon' question, likely voters: cost of living 18%, high taxes 16%, homelessness 13%, housing affordability 10%, economy/jobs 8%, education 7%, government spending 7%, addiction/mental health 5%, environment/climate/wildfires 5%. Ties broken by the registered-voter figures. Excluded as not testable by a vote: poor leadership (11%), Democrats/one-party rule (9%), and Trump/federal government/ICE (5%, mainly about a person/party). Rank 10 is health care (4% open-ended; 67% of likely voters called it very important in the same poll's closed question). Question asks about Oregon's problems; state and national issues ranked together.

issues.detail: Lower family costs; take on corporate monopolies and billionaire interests.
Repeal Republican-passed tax breaks that mainly benefit the wealthy; make billionaires and corporations pay more.
Keep the 2026 law barring hedge funds from buying more single-family homes (already law).
Data centers, if built, use union labor; federal AI rules on oversight and transparency.
Invest more in education and infrastructure instead of foreign wars and bases.
Use Budget Committee role to reduce national debt; cut wasteful defense spending.
Require data centers to run on renewable electricity with conservation measures; oppose clean-energy rollbacks.
Pass his bills removing hedge funds/private equity from health care; U.S. drug prices equal to other developed nations.

plan_caveats: Merkley ran a thin, democracy-focused campaign (anti-Trump, filibuster, dark money); no 2026 debate, Ballotpedia survey, or detailed plan release was found. Most positions come from one KATU interview (Oct 23, 2026) and one OPB profile (Oct 14, 2026).
Campaign issues page (jeffmerkley.com/issues, 'Our Fight') could not be fetched; two campaign blog posts (Dec 2025, Feb 2026) were read and contained no specifics.
Taxes rated Concrete as a repeal, but the law is not named (likely 2017/2025 GOP tax law provisions for high earners and corporations); grade on votes to repeal those breaks.

Health care bill identified by researcher: KATU interview only says 'bills to get the hedge funds out of the healthcare system'; the 2026 bill he backed is the Take Back Our Hospitals Act (no Medicare payments to private-equity-owned hospitals/nursing homes, https://www.merkley.senate.gov/?p=24244).
Housing rated Partial because the hedge-fund home-buying ban he cites already passed in 2026; no new housing commitment found.
Jobs and climate details come from his answer on federal data-center rules; he also said communities should decide on data centers, so these are approaches, not checkable mandates.

Ending the Iran war ('need a majority that will end it') is a clear 2026 commitment but does not map to a top-10 issue; he links the war to the national debt (spending, rank 7) without making it the stated fix.
Clean-energy rollback opposition is from his July 2025 campaign launch, not a 2026 statement.
Senate-office town halls from 2023-2024 found in searches were excluded as past record.
